candidate_sources.title: Brown Rot Blossom Blight / Almond / Agriculture: Pest Management Guidelines / UC Statewide IPM Program (UC IPM)
candidate_sources.snippet: Brown rot in almonds is caused by Monilinia laxa, with M. fructicola occurring rarely. Young blossom spurs and associated leaves collapse to form shoot blight; gum may exude at the base of infected flowers. Management is achieved through fungicides applied at bloom and sanitation of mummified fruit and infected twigs.

candidate_sources.title: Brown Rot of Stone Fruits : Landscape : Center for Agriculture, Food, and the Environment (CAFE) at UMass Amherst
candidate_sources.snippet: Brown rot is caused by Monilinia species (M. fructicola, M. laxa, M. fructigena). Infected blossoms turn brown and wilt; fruit develops brown spots that expand and become covered with powdery tan masses of spores. The fungus overwinters in mummified fruit and twig cankers.

candidate_sources.title: Brown Rot Blossom and Twig Blight / Home and Landscape / UC Statewide IPM Program (UC IPM)
candidate_sources.snippet: At high humidity, gray to tan spore masses form on diseased flower parts and twig cankers. Cankers on blighted twigs have tan centers with dark margins. The fungus survives in twig cankers and on remaining diseased flower parts; spore pads (sporodochia) appear in late winter to provide inoculum for spring infection. Infection is favored by rainy weather with temperatures in the mid-70s during bloom.
diseases_mentioned: Brown rot blossom and twig blight

candidate_sources.title: Shot Hole, or Coryneum Blight / Home and Landscape / UC Statewide IPM Program (UC IPM)
candidate_sources.snippet: Shot hole first appears in spring as purplish or reddish spots about 1/10 inch in diameter on new buds, leaves, and shoots. Spots on young leaves commonly have a narrow, light green or yellow margin. The spots expand and their centers turn brown and can drop out, leaving holes. Caused by the fungus Wilsonomyces carpophilus. Management combines pruning out infected tissue and fungicide (fixed copper or Bordeaux) applications.

candidate_sources.snippet: SHOT HOLE OF ALMOND (AL16005). Shot hole, caused by Stigmina carpophila (syn. Wilsonomyces carpophilus), produces reddish-brown leaf lesions that drop out leaving holes, and lesions on twigs and fruit. Temperature and duration of leaf wetness influence development of shot-hole disease on almond leaves.

candidate_sources.title: Coryneum or Shothole Blight | USU Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Coryneum blight, or shot hole disease, is a fungal infection caused by the pathogen Wilsonomyces carpophilus. Almond, apricot, nectarine, peach, plum and cherry trees can be affected. Symptoms begin as small reddish/purplish-brown spots that dry up and fall away leaving BB-sized holes. The fungus overwinters in infected twigs and buds and becomes active during wet, warm spring conditions.

candidate_sources.title: Shot Hole Fungus on Almond â€” The Almond Doctor
candidate_sources.snippet: Shot hole fungus (Wilsonomyces carpophilus, formerly Stigmina carpophila) infects almond leaves, twigs and fruit. Lesions on fruit are purplish-brown, slightly corky and raised; severe infection can kill the developing nut or cause deformities affecting quality.
